### Bug Scenario Image Analysis & Root Cause Reasoning

The image shows an F# code snippet where the use of `Operators.(*)` is incorrectly causing the syntax highlighter to treat the rest of the code as a multi-line comment. In F#, multi-line comments are denoted by `(* ... *)`. The bug is that the highlighter is matching the `(*` in `Operators.(*)` as the start of a comment, which is incorrect.

**Root Cause:**  
The regex for multi-line comments in the F# highlighter is too permissive and matches any `(*`, even when it appears as part of an identifier or operator, such as `Operators.(*)`. It should only match `(*` when it is not immediately preceded by a `.` (dot), which is how F# allows operator overloading.

---

### Bug Code Snippet Analysis

The relevant code is in `src/languages/fsharp.js`:
```javascript
hljs.COMMENT('\\(\\*', '\\*\\)')
```
This matches any `(* ... *)` sequence, regardless of context.

---

### Patch

We need to update the comment regex so that it does **not** match `(*` when it is immediately preceded by a `.` (dot). This can be done using a negative lookbehind in the regex: `(?<!\.)\(\*`.

**Note:** Negative lookbehind is supported in modern JavaScript engines.

---

```javascript
### src/languages/fsharp.js
<<<<<<< SEARCH
      hljs.COMMENT('\\(\\*', '\\*\\)'),
=======
      hljs.COMMENT('(?<!\\.)\\(\\*', '\\*\\)'),
>>>>>>> REPLACE
```

---

**Explanation:**  
- The regex `(?<!\.)\(\*` ensures that `(*` is only matched as a comment start if it is **not** immediately preceded by a dot, thus preventing false positives in cases like `Operators.(*)`.

This patch will fix the bug as described in the report and shown in the image.
